The respondent police after completing the investigation filed a final report before the learned Judicial Magistrate, Andipatti, and the same was taken on file in C.C.No.221 of 2011.

At this stage, the petitioner came to know that the Investigation Officer without conducting proper investigation, filed the final report.
3. According to the petitioner, the Investigation Officer not even obtained hand writing expert opinion.
The case of the petitioner is that the accused forged his signature and created a document relating to his property.

So, a case was registered https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis for the offences punishable under Sections 419,

Hence, the duty of the Investigation Officer is to obtain hand writing expert opinion to prove the case of the prosecution.
The same was not done by the Investigation Officer.
So, he filed a petition in Crl.MP.No.7075 of 2019 under Section 173 (8) Cr.P.C before the learned Judicial Magistrate, Theni, and the same was returned as 'not maintainable'.
Hence, he filed Crl.OP(MD)No.350 of 2020 before this Court.

Hence, this Court is inclined to allow this revision in the following terms:-
i) The order passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Theni, Theni District, in Crl.MP.No.7075 of 2019 dated 03.05.2023, is hereby set aside and remit back to the learned Judicial Magistrate, Theni, to pass order on merits.
